sanskrit_verse: यच् छिष्टं पितृदायेभ्यो दत्त्वा ऋणं पैतृकं च यत् । भ्रातृभिस् तद् विभक्तव्यम् ऋणी न स्याद् यथा पिता ॥
transliteration: yac chiṣṭaṃ pitṛdāyebhyo dattvā rṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ ca yat | bhrātṛbhis tad vibhaktavyam ṛṇī na syād yatha pitā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: What remains after fulfilling obligations to those entitled by ancestral duty, and the debt owed to parents, must be divided among brothers. In this division, none shall remain liable as debtor beyond what was received from the father.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from the Source of sustenance and continuity
Causation arises through relational dharmic obligation, not individual will
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by receipt and alignment with origin
Restoration logic operates through proportional return to source integrity
Consciousness alignment occurs when relational debts are dissolved without residue
executable_legal_axioms: IF an heir receives property AFTER fulfillment of Pitru-debts AND ancestral obligations THEN that heir's liability is limited to their share of the remaining estate
IF a brother has fulfilled his portion of shared parental debt THEN no further personal liability attaches beyond received inheritance
IF division of assets mirrors original receipt THEN no party becomes a debtor post-distribution
IF all parties align with Pitru-dharma in distribution THEN collective liberation from indebtedness is assured
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that filial or fraternal liability cannot exceed the scope of benefit received after ancestral duties are discharged. The threshold of responsibility is tied not to blood relation but to conscious participation in dharma-aligned succession. Authority derives from alignment with Pitru-dharma, not legal fiction of ownership.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that cause lies in the act of receiving within a dharmic framework. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that debt manifests sequentially—first to ancestors, then among successors. Proportional responsibility ensures that no one bears more than their aligned share. Non-punitive reality is upheld because liability ends upon correct alignment with the source-debt resolution.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate family council under Vedic witness to affirm Pitru-debt completion
Execute asset division mirroring original dharmic entitlements
Establish individual declarations of non-liability once proportional receipt confirmed
Reintegrate fraternal bonds through reciprocal release of residual claim
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails where relational duty concludes and equitable sharing begins; neither punishment nor perpetual liability may arise where consciousness aligns with Pitru-dharma. Reality itself enforces completion.
